Move related platform definitions and data between environments as explicit, inspectable packages.

What it owns

  • Package and package-item APIs.
  • Export orchestration for content, documents, workflow, app security and related domains.
  • Import hooks that publish package events to domain owners.

Why the boundary matters

Configuration and content migration becomes a governed process instead of a collection of unrepeatable database scripts.

How it fits

The domain is published and tested independently, then composed through cCoder.Core when an application needs the complete platform. That keeps ownership visible while preserving a straightforward application bootstrap.

Getting started

The source, current README, sample hosts and tests live in cCoder.Packaging on GitHub. The repository README is the version-specific starting point; the outline below explains how the pieces fit together.

Reference the package

<PackageReference Include="cCoder.Packaging" Version="YOUR_VERSION" />

During coordinated local development the repositories may substitute a sibling ProjectReference. Published applications should normally consume the agreed package version so the dependency boundary remains explicit.

Register it in the host

builder.Services.AddPackagingWeb();
// or builder.Services.AddPackaging() in a non-Web composition.

Configure and run it

Register the package managers for the domains the host can export and import. Each domain remains responsible for interpreting its own package items and reacting to package-import events.

Consume the capability

Create Package and PackageItem records, invoke the domain export orchestration, and import through the governed package flow. Treat packages as inspectable migration units—not as an excuse to copy database rows between environments.

Build and verify from source

git clone https://github.com/ccoder-co-uk/cCoder.Packaging.git
cd cCoder.Packaging
dotnet build
dotnet test

Use the repository-specific solution and test commands from its README when working on the domain itself; the standalone and acceptance-test hosts show the supported application boundary more accurately than an isolated snippet can.
